name: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari
nameAr: عبد الله بن قيس بن سليم بن حضار الأشعري، أبو موسى، رضي الله عنه
diedNote: 50 AH, or later (Taqrib); the Shamela record collects 42, 44, 49, 51, 52 and 53
residence: Zabid and Adan (governor for the Prophet ﷺ)

students.name: Qays ibn Abi Hazim
students.source: Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (as cited on the linked record)

companionCounts.source: Totals: al-Khazraji, Khulasat Tadhhib Tahdhib al-Kamal, p. 210 (360 hadith; 50 agreed upon; 4 in al-Bukhari alone; 25 in Muslim alone). In al-Bukhari: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 10 (57)

bio: A Yemeni Companion who came to Islam early and whom the Prophet ﷺ set over Zabid and Adan. Umar made him governor of Basra and Uthman of Kufa, and he was one of the two arbitrators after Siffin (Taqrib). The Prophet ﷺ said of his recitation that he had been given one of the flutes of the family of Dawud (Sahih al-Bukhari 5048). Al-Khazraji counts 360 hadith from him, 50 of them agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim. He appears in two of the hadith studied here, once through his son Abu Burdah and once through the Kufan Successor Abu Wa'il.
